<!-- ===== BEGIN prompts/extensions/creator-reference-locked-prompts.md ===== -->

# Creator Prompts Using Your Own Character Reference

This builds directly on `CREATOR-00`/`CREATOR-01`/`CREATOR-02` (the general creator-style prompts). The difference here: instead of describing a creator from scratch, you attach **your own reference photo of a real person** (yourself, a client, hired talent) and the prompt locks that exact face/identity in place while generating new poses, settings, and lighting around it.

**Required before you use any of this:** a real photo, and **documented consent** from that person to generate AI images of their likeness. This is not optional and not something any prompt or tool can verify for you — confirm it yourself before generating anything. If the reference is a public figure or anyone other than you, get that confirmed in writing.

**A practical limitation to expect:** several image models restrict or outright refuse generating photoreal images of real, identifiable people from a single reference photo — this is a deliberate policy guardrail against impersonation/deepfakes, not a prompt-wording problem. If a model refuses or the identity doesn't carry over reliably, that's a tool/policy limitation, not something to "prompt-engineer around" — you may need a tool explicitly built for consented identity-preservation (and that still verifies consent on its end). `CREATOR-REF-00` below includes a test step specifically to catch this early, before you build a whole shot list around a reference that won't actually hold.

---

## `CREATOR-REF-00` v1.0 — Lock In Your Character's Identity (prep step — do this first)

**Purpose:** Confirm your reference photo can actually be used as a reliable identity lock before generating a full set of scenes from it — one small test generation instead of discovering the problem after building everything else.

**Required inputs:** the reference photo; confirmation that consent is documented.

**Prompt:**
```
ROLE: You generate a single confirmation image to test whether this
reference photo's identity can be reliably preserved before further use.

IDENTITY REFERENCE: [attached photo] — preserve facial structure, features,
and proportions exactly, per REF-01 conventions. This role outranks every
other instruction in this prompt.

TASK: Generate the same person, same framing and angle as the reference,
in a plain neutral setting with even, neutral lighting — no stylistic
changes. This is a fidelity check, not a creative shot.
```

**Quality check:** Compare the output directly against the reference photo. Does it read as unmistakably the same person — same facial structure, proportions, distinguishing features? If it's a "similar-looking" generic person rather than that specific individual, stop here: this model/workflow isn't preserving identity reliably enough for production use. Try a tool built specifically for consented identity/face preservation instead of plain text-to-image.

**Common failure:** the model generates someone who resembles the reference in general terms (age, hair, build) but not in the specific facial structure that makes them recognizable as that individual — easy to miss at a glance, so compare side-by-side, not from memory.

---

## `CREATOR-REF-01` v1.0 — Seated, Mid-Gesture Shot (your character)

**Purpose:** The `CREATOR-01` seated/gesturing creator shot, built around your specific reference identity instead of a described one.

**Required inputs:** the confirmed reference photo (passed `CREATOR-REF-00`); wardrobe; setting; lighting mood.

**Prompt:**
```
ROLE: You generate a single, highly photorealistic still image of a content
creator mid-explanation, filmed for a talking-head YouTube/podcast segment.

IDENTITY REFERENCE: [attached, confirmed reference photo] — preserve facial
structure, features, and proportions exactly. This is the same individual
as the reference, not a new or similar-looking person. Everything else in
this prompt (wardrobe, pose, setting, lighting) may change freely.

WARDROBE: [e.g., an oversized, relaxed crewneck sweatshirt, jeans, mic
clipped to the collar]
POSE: seated in a modern upholstered accent chair, legs casually crossed,
both hands raised at chest height mid-gesture as if explaining a point —
natural, unposed hand positions
SETTING: [e.g., a warm, cozy home-studio living-room corner — framed art,
plants, a softly glowing floor lamp, a shelf with small decor items]
LIGHTING: warm, neutral daylight-balanced key light, soft and even on the
face, shallow depth of field blurring the background
CAMERA: eye-level, vertical 9:16 framing, medium-wide shot showing the full
seated figure

[Insert Photorealism Reinforcement Block from the main Creator Prompts doc]
```

**Expected output:** a vertical, photoreal seated creator shot — the specific reference identity, in a new pose/setting.

**Quality check:** run the same side-by-side identity comparison as `CREATOR-REF-00` before accepting — don't assume a successful first shot means every future shot from this reference will hold. Also check hands (this pose is hand-heavy) and that no wardrobe/background text is garbled.

**Common failure:** identity holds in a straightforward, front-facing shot but drifts once a more dynamic pose or different lighting is requested — if so, simplify the pose/lighting change and reintroduce complexity gradually rather than changing everything at once.

**Follow-ups:**
- "Regenerate keeping the identity and pose identical, change only [wardrobe/setting/lighting element]."
- "Diagnose which facial feature drifted from the reference, then regenerate."

---

## `CREATOR-REF-02` v1.0 — Close-Up, Presenting an Object (your character)

**Purpose:** The `CREATOR-02` close-up/presenting creator shot, built around your specific reference identity.

**Required inputs:** the confirmed reference photo; the object being presented; lighting mood.

**Prompt:**
```
ROLE: You generate a single, highly photorealistic close-up still image of
a content creator presenting an object directly to camera, filmed for a
talking-head review/vlog-style video segment.

IDENTITY REFERENCE: [attached, confirmed reference photo] — preserve facial
structure, features, and proportions exactly. This is the same individual
as the reference, not a new or similar-looking person.

ACTION: holding [PROP] up toward the camera with both hands, roughly chest-
to-face height, as if actively showing/reviewing it, mouth open mid-
sentence, direct eye contact with camera
FRAMING: tight chest-up close-up, the object prominent in the lower-middle
of frame, face clearly visible above it
SETTING: [e.g., a dim, moody room with a blurred shelf of books/objects in
the background]
LIGHTING: [e.g., warm amber/red accent lighting as the dominant tone, a
single key light on the face from the front]
CAMERA: eye-level, close distance, vertical 9:16 framing, shallow depth of
field, background details indistinct

[Insert Photorealism Reinforcement Block from the main Creator Prompts doc]
```

**Expected output:** a vertical, close-up photoreal still of the specific reference identity presenting an object to camera.

**Quality check:** identity comparison as above; also zoom into the held object's label/cover text, which is the most common place for garbled text to appear — regenerate the object only if needed, keeping identity and pose identical.

**Follow-ups:**
- "Regenerate only the object, keep identity, pose, and lighting identical — the label text is garbled."
- "Change only the lighting mood, keep identity and pose identical."

---

## Keeping it consistent across a whole shot list

Once `CREATOR-REF-00` confirms the reference holds reliably:
1. Reuse the **exact same reference photo** for every subsequent shot — don't regenerate or "refresh" the identity reference between shots, which reintroduces drift risk.
2. After each new shot, do a quick side-by-side check against the original reference, not against the previous generated shot (errors compound if you check against the last output instead of the source).
3. Keep a short log of which shots passed/failed the identity check — if a particular pose or lighting style reliably causes drift, avoid that combination rather than retrying it repeatedly.
4. If you're publishing this content as advertising or in a context where it could be mistaken for the real person's live appearance, check current platform policy on AI-generated likeness disclosure — separate from the generation process itself.

<!-- ===== END prompts/extensions/creator-reference-locked-prompts.md ===== -->

<!-- ===== BEGIN prompts/extensions/creator-prompts-standalone.md ===== -->

# Creator Prompts — Standalone Copy-Paste Library

Each prompt below is fully self-contained — copy the whole code block, nothing else needed.

---

## 1. Master Creator Talking-Head Template

**Purpose:** A reusable base prompt for generating a photorealistic "content creator" talking-to-camera photo in any setting/wardrobe/mood you fill in.

```
ROLE: You generate a single, highly photorealistic still image of a content
creator filming a talking-to-camera video segment (YouTube/podcast/vlog
style) — polished but authentic, not a phone-shot candid, not a commercial
studio ad.

CREATOR: [describe appearance]
WARDROBE: [describe wardrobe]
SETTING: [describe a lived-in, intentionally decorated space]
FRAMING: [seated-wide / close-up chest-up]
ACTION: [e.g., "mid-sentence, both hands raised in an explaining gesture"
or "holding [PROP] up toward camera with both hands, presenting it"]
LIGHTING: [e.g., "warm, neutral daylight-balanced key light from one side,
soft fill" or "warm amber/red moody accent lighting, single key light"]
MIC: a small lavalier microphone clipped to the collar, visibly present but
not the focus
CAMERA: eye-level with the subject, as if on a tripod a few feet away,
vertical 9:16 framing, shallow depth of field with the background
softly blurred

REALISM REQUIREMENTS:
- Natural skin texture: visible pores, slight unevenness, natural oil/shine
  on forehead and nose — not airbrushed or plastic-smooth.
- Natural facial asymmetry — avoid a perfectly symmetrical, "generated"-
  looking face.
- Realistic eyes: natural catchlights from the room's actual light sources,
  slight redness/moisture, not glassy or waxy.
- Shot on a mirrorless camera, 35mm or 50mm lens, at a wide aperture
  (f/1.8–f/2.8) — natural falloff and background blur, not a synthetic/
  uniform blur.
- Lighting should behave physically: shadows fall consistently from the
  stated light sources, skin tones respond naturally to warm/cool light
  mixing in the room.
- Natural hand anatomy — correct finger count and proportion.

AVOID: airbrushed/plastic skin, waxy or glassy eyes, perfectly symmetrical
features, "uncanny valley" smoothness, garbled text on any visible object
or background text/labels, extra or malformed fingers.
```

---

## 2. Seated Talking-Head, Mid-Gesture

**Purpose:** A specific, ready-to-run version of the creator template — seated, cross-legged, gesturing mid-explanation, cozy warm living-room setting.

```
ROLE: You generate a single, highly photorealistic still image of a content
creator mid-explanation, filmed for a talking-head YouTube/podcast segment.

CREATOR: an East Asian man in his early-to-mid 30s, short-to-medium wavy
dark hair, clean-shaven, warm approachable expression, mouth slightly open
mid-sentence
WARDROBE: an oversized, relaxed beige/cream crewneck sweatshirt, blue denim
jeans, white sneakers, small lavalier mic clipped to the collar
POSE: seated in a modern upholstered accent chair, legs casually crossed,
both hands raised at chest height mid-gesture as if explaining a point —
natural, unposed hand positions
SETTING: a warm, cozy home-studio living-room corner — a framed botanical
leaf print on the wall, potted plants, a floor lamp glowing softly on the
left, a shelf in the background with candles, small boxes, and a vase,
wood flooring with a patterned rug
FOREGROUND: a small round wooden side table at bottom-left with a plain
ceramic mug sitting on it, slightly soft-focused since it's closer to camera
LIGHTING: warm, neutral daylight-balanced key light from the front-left,
soft and even on the face, warm practical lamp glow in the background,
shallow depth of field blurring the background softly
CAMERA: eye-level, as if on a tripod several feet away, vertical 9:16
framing, medium-wide shot showing the full seated figure

REALISM REQUIREMENTS:
- Natural skin texture: visible pores, slight unevenness, natural oil/shine
  on forehead and nose — not airbrushed or plastic-smooth.
- Natural facial asymmetry — avoid a perfectly symmetrical, "generated"-
  looking face.
- Realistic eyes: natural catchlights from the room's actual light sources,
  slight redness/moisture, not glassy or waxy.
- Shot on a mirrorless camera, 35mm or 50mm lens, at a wide aperture
  (f/1.8–f/2.8) — natural falloff and background blur, not a synthetic/
  uniform blur.
- Lighting should behave physically: shadows fall consistently from the
  stated light sources, skin tones respond naturally to warm/cool light
  mixing in the room.
- Natural hand anatomy — correct finger count and proportion, especially
  important here since both hands are raised and expressive.

AVOID: airbrushed/plastic skin, waxy or glassy eyes, perfectly symmetrical
features, "uncanny valley" smoothness, garbled text on any visible object
or background text/labels, extra or malformed fingers.
```

---

## 3. Close-Up, Presenting an Object to Camera

**Purpose:** A specific, ready-to-run creator shot — tight close-up, holding/presenting a product or book to camera, moody warm lighting.

```
ROLE: You generate a single, highly photorealistic close-up still image of
a content creator presenting an object directly to camera, filmed for a
talking-head review/vlog-style video segment.

CREATOR: a man in his late 20s to early 30s, light-medium skin tone,
brown wavy/curly hair, light stubble beard, engaged expression, mouth open
mid-sentence as if explaining the object, direct eye contact with the camera
WARDROBE: a plain black crew-neck T-shirt or sweatshirt, a smartwatch visible
on one wrist
ACTION: holding [the object being presented] up toward the camera with both
hands, roughly chest-to-face height, as if actively showing/reviewing it
FRAMING: tight chest-up close-up, the object prominent in the lower-middle
of frame, face clearly visible above it
SETTING: a dim, moody room — a blurred wooden shelf lined with books and a
few dark decorative objects in the background
LIGHTING: warm amber/red accent lighting as the dominant tone, a single key
light on the face from the front, dim ambient fill, noticeable warm color
cast consistent across skin and background
CAMERA: eye-level, close distance, vertical 9:16 framing, shallow depth of
field with the background softly blurred, background shelf details
indistinct

REALISM REQUIREMENTS:
- Natural skin texture: visible pores, slight unevenness, natural oil/shine
  on forehead and nose — not airbrushed or plastic-smooth.
- Natural facial asymmetry — avoid a perfectly symmetrical, "generated"-
  looking face.
- Realistic eyes: natural catchlights from the room's actual light sources,
  slight redness/moisture, not glassy or waxy.
- Shot on a mirrorless camera, 35mm or 50mm lens, at a wide aperture
  (f/1.8–f/2.8) — natural falloff and background blur, not a synthetic/
  uniform blur.
- Lighting should behave physically: shadows fall consistently from the
  stated light sources, skin tones respond naturally to warm/cool light
  mixing in the room.
- Natural hand anatomy — correct finger count and proportion.
- Any visible text/label on the held object must be legible and correctly
  spelled, not garbled.

AVOID: airbrushed/plastic skin, waxy or glassy eyes, perfectly symmetrical
features, "uncanny valley" smoothness, garbled text on any visible object
or background text/labels, extra or malformed fingers.
```

---

## 4. Lock In a Real Person's Identity (prep step)

**Purpose:** Test whether a specific reference photo of a real person can be reliably reused before building a full shot list around it. Requires the real person's documented consent to generate/use their likeness.

```
ROLE: You generate a single confirmation image to test whether this
reference photo's identity can be reliably preserved before further use.

IDENTITY REFERENCE: [attached photo] — preserve facial structure, features,
and proportions exactly. This role outranks every other instruction in
this prompt.

TASK: Generate the same person, same framing and angle as the reference,
in a plain neutral setting with even, neutral lighting — no stylistic
changes. This is a fidelity check, not a creative shot.
```

---

## 5. Seated Mid-Gesture Shot Using a Real Person's Reference

**Purpose:** The seated/gesturing creator shot, built around a specific confirmed real-person reference photo instead of a described identity. Requires documented consent.

```
ROLE: You generate a single, highly photorealistic still image of a content
creator mid-explanation, filmed for a talking-head YouTube/podcast segment.

IDENTITY REFERENCE: [attached, confirmed reference photo] — preserve facial
structure, features, and proportions exactly. This is the same individual
as the reference, not a new or similar-looking person. Everything else in
this prompt (wardrobe, pose, setting, lighting) may change freely.

WARDROBE: [e.g., an oversized, relaxed crewneck sweatshirt, jeans, mic
clipped to the collar]
POSE: seated in a modern upholstered accent chair, legs casually crossed,
both hands raised at chest height mid-gesture as if explaining a point —
natural, unposed hand positions
SETTING: [e.g., a warm, cozy home-studio living-room corner — framed art,
plants, a softly glowing floor lamp, a shelf with small decor items]
LIGHTING: warm, neutral daylight-balanced key light, soft and even on the
face, shallow depth of field blurring the background
CAMERA: eye-level, vertical 9:16 framing, medium-wide shot showing the full
seated figure

REALISM REQUIREMENTS:
- Natural skin texture: visible pores, slight unevenness, natural oil/shine
  on forehead and nose — not airbrushed or plastic-smooth.
- Natural facial asymmetry — avoid a perfectly symmetrical, "generated"-
  looking face.
- Realistic eyes: natural catchlights from the room's actual light sources,
  slight redness/moisture, not glassy or waxy.
- Shot on a mirrorless camera, 35mm or 50mm lens, at a wide aperture
  (f/1.8–f/2.8) — natural falloff and background blur, not a synthetic/
  uniform blur.
- Natural hand anatomy — correct finger count and proportion.

AVOID: airbrushed/plastic skin, waxy or glassy eyes, perfectly symmetrical
features, "uncanny valley" smoothness, garbled text, extra or malformed
fingers, and any drift away from the reference identity's facial structure.
```

<!-- ===== BEGIN prompts/extensions/ugc-avatar-prompts.md ===== -->

# UGC-Style & Digital-Human Avatar Image Prompts

**Important — read before using:** These prompts are **newly written for this request** — they are **not** part of the original 8-part AI Creative Operating System library. I checked the original image-generation library (Part 5) and it contains no prompt literally called "UGC" or "Avatar"; the only existing adjacent content is `IP-06` (Photoreal lifestyle image), `IP-03`/`IP-04` (Character design/pose variation), `CC-01` (Character Consistency), `IP-11` (Thumbnail/social ad visual), and `REF-01` (Reference Engineering). The prompts below were built fresh, in the same format as the rest of the library, specifically for:
1. **UGC-style content images** — photos meant to read as authentic, unpolished, user-generated content (not studio-produced).
2. **Avatar prompts = photoreal AI digital humans** — a synthetic spokesperson/talking-head identity meant to be reused consistently across an ad or video campaign (per your clarification).

They follow the same `STD-00` shape as the original library (ID, Purpose, Required Inputs, Prompt, Expected Output, Quality Check, Follow-ups) and reuse the original library's conventions where relevant (`REF-01` reference roles, `CC-01` consistency checks). They have **not** been tested against specific model adapters the way the original library's prompts were — treat the bracketed model suggestions as starting points, not verified routing.

**A compliance note that applies to every prompt below (read once, applies throughout):** Synthetic "UGC" and "digital human/avatar" content sits in an area with real legal and platform-policy exposure:
- If an avatar/digital human is meant to be **fully synthetic** (no real person behind it), say so explicitly in the prompt and verify the output doesn't accidentally resemble an identifiable real person (especially a public figure) before using it in paid media.
- If it's based on a **real person's likeness**, you need that person's documented consent before generating or using the content — this is not something the image model can verify for you.
- Several ad platforms (Meta, TikTok, YouTube/Google) and some jurisdictions require **disclosure when content is AI-generated or features a synthetic person**, especially in advertising or testimonial-style content. Check current platform policy and local advertising law before publishing — this library can't confirm current rules for you.
- None of this is enforced by the image model itself; it's a human review step you need to keep in your process.

---

## Section A — UGC-Style Content Image Prompts

### `UGC-01` v1.0 — UGC-Style Product/Lifestyle Photo

**Purpose:** Generate a single still image that reads as authentic, non-produced user-generated content — the kind of photo a real customer would post, not a brand's studio shot.

**Use when:** the brief calls for an "authentic," "organic," or "native-feeling" image for social/ad placements where a polished look would undercut credibility.

**Don't use when:** the deliverable needs to look like professional brand photography — use `IP-06` (Photoreal lifestyle image) instead.

**Required inputs:** `SUBJECT_OR_PRODUCT`, `ENVIRONMENT`/setting, target platform (e.g., Instagram feed, TikTok, Reels cover).

**Prompt:**
```
ROLE: You generate a single still image that must read as authentic,
unpolished user-generated content — not professional or brand photography.

SUBJECT: [SUBJECT_OR_PRODUCT]
SETTING: [ENVIRONMENT — a real, everyday location, not a studio]
PLATFORM: [target platform, for aspect ratio/framing conventions]

REQUIREMENTS:
- Composition should feel casual and slightly imperfect — off-center framing,
  a natural (not centered/symmetrical) crop, like someone quickly took the shot.
- Lighting must be ambient/available light only (window light, indoor lamp,
  daylight) — no studio lighting, softboxes, or rim lighting language.
- Use "phone camera" visual language: natural depth of field a phone camera
  produces, slight imperfection acceptable (not professional bokeh control).
- Do not add overt branding, polish, or graphic design elements — this is a
  photo, not an ad layout.
- State plainly if any people are synthetic (no real-world counterpart) or
  if this depicts a real, consented subject — do not leave this ambiguous.

AVOID: tripod-stable framing, symmetrical composition, studio lighting setups,
camera/lens language associated with commercial photography (e.g., "85mm
portrait lens, softbox key light"), an overly "produced" result.
```

**Expected output:** a single image that could plausibly have been taken by a real person on a phone, featuring the subject/product in a real-feeling setting.

**Quality check:** Does this still look "produced" or "commercial" despite the casual wording? If yes, reject and push harder on imperfection (see follow-ups). Confirm the synthetic-vs-real-person disclosure question above was actually answered, not skipped.

**Common failure:** image models default toward polished, well-composed results even when asked for "casual" — the commercial-photography training bias tends to win unless explicitly fought.

**Follow-ups:**
- "Make the framing more off-center and less composed, like a quick phone photo."
- "Add a slight reflection or glare, like a real phone camera in this lighting."
- "Reduce the production quality — this should look like a candid snapshot, not a shoot."

---

### `UGC-02` v1.0 — UGC-Style Testimonial / Selfie Portrait

**Purpose:** A believable "customer selfie" or testimonial-style portrait of a person holding or using a product — for a static UGC-style ad image, or as a base frame feeding a UGC-style video.

**Use when:** the brief needs a "real customer" look for a testimonial, review-style ad, or before/after post.

**Required inputs:** either (a) a description of a fully synthetic person [age range, general styling — described, not based on anyone real], or (b) a real reference photo **with documented consent on file**; product reference; platform/aspect ratio.

**Prompt:**
```
ROLE: You generate a single testimonial/selfie-style portrait that reads
as a real customer photo, not a staged or professional portrait.

PERSON: [EITHER: "a fully synthetic person, no real-world counterpart —
describe only general, non-identifying styling: age range, general look" |
OR: "based on attached reference photo of [NAME], consent on file dated
[DATE]"] — state explicitly which case applies; do not leave this blank.
PRODUCT: [product reference — preserve exact geometry/branding if a real
product]
SETTING: [a plausible everyday location for a selfie: bathroom, car,
bedroom, kitchen]
PLATFORM: [target platform/aspect ratio]

REQUIREMENTS:
- Selfie-style framing: arm's-length or near-arm's-length distance, slightly
  elevated or straight-on angle, not a professional portrait setup.
- Expression should look natural/candid, not posed or commercial.
- Lighting: ordinary room/available light, not studio lighting.
- If the product is real, preserve its exact packaging/label/logo — do not
  invent or alter branding details.

AVOID: studio lighting, professional posing, airbrushed/retouched skin
texture, perfectly centered symmetrical framing.
```

**Expected output:** a single selfie-style portrait image with the product visible, looking like an authentic customer photo.

**Quality check:** If "fully synthetic" was specified, does the face resemble any identifiable real/public person? If so, regenerate — do not use. If based on a real person, confirm consent documentation exists before use, separately from this prompt.

**Common failure:** the model generates a face that coincidentally resembles a recognizable public figure even with no reference supplied — always visually cross-check before use in paid media.

**Follow-ups:**
- "Regenerate the face only, keep the same pose, framing, and product position."
- "Make this look more like a quick, unplanned selfie rather than a posed photo."
- "Diagnose which facial feature reads as recognizable/too specific, then regenerate with more generic styling."

---

### `UGC-03` v1.0 — UGC-Style Unboxing / Product-in-Hand Close-Up

**Purpose:** A close, casual shot of hands holding, unwrapping, or using a product — a common UGC ad format (unboxing, close-up demo).

**Use when:** the format calls for a hands-on, close-up "real person using the product" shot rather than a full-scene lifestyle photo.

**Required inputs:** real product reference (geometry/branding must come from a real photo, not invented), setting/surface description.

**Prompt:**
```
ROLE: You generate a close-up, casual "hands-on" product shot in the style
of an unboxing or demo clip still — not a studio product shot.

PRODUCT: [reference image — preserve exact packaging, logo, and geometry]
ACTION: [unboxing / holding / applying / demonstrating — be specific]
SURFACE_OR_SETTING: [e.g., kitchen counter, bed, car seat — an ordinary,
real-feeling surface, not a seamless studio backdrop]

REQUIREMENTS:
- Framing: close, slightly cropped, as if captured mid-action rather than
  composed — hands and product should dominate the frame.
- Lighting: ordinary indoor/available light, not studio lighting.
- Preserve the product's real packaging and branding exactly as referenced.
- Minor visual imperfection (slight blur, uneven framing) is acceptable and
  often desirable for authenticity.

AVOID: seamless studio backdrops, perfectly centered product placement,
invented or altered logos/label text.
```

**Expected output:** a close, casual image of hands interacting with the real product, in a plausible everyday setting.

**Quality check:** Run the same check as `PC-01` (Product Consistency) on the packaging/logo — zoom to full resolution and confirm no label text or logo was altered or misspelled.

**Common failure:** label/logo text is subtly re-rendered or distorted on small packaging — easy to miss at thumbnail size.

**Follow-ups:**
- "Regenerate only the background/surface, keep the product and hand position identical."
- "Zoom in tighter / pull back slightly" (framing adjustment only).

---

## Section B — Digital-Human Avatar Prompts (Photoreal, for Video/Ads)

### `AVA-01` v1.0 — Digital Human Base Identity (Spokesperson Avatar)

**Purpose:** Establish a single, locked, photoreal **synthetic** "digital human" identity to be reused consistently as an AI spokesperson/avatar across a campaign — the base reference everything else (poses, talking-head frames, video) gets generated from.

**Use when:** you need a recurring AI-generated person (spokesperson, host, reviewer-style presenter) for ads or UGC-style video, and no real person is being depicted.

**Don't use when:** the "avatar" is meant to represent a real, specific person — that requires documented consent and a real reference photo, not this prompt.

**Required inputs:** campaign/brand descriptor, general (non-identifying) styling direction — age range, general look, wardrobe style; explicit confirmation this is fully synthetic.

**Prompt:**
```
ROLE: You generate a single, neutral reference image establishing a fully
synthetic digital-human identity. This person does not represent, and must
not resemble, any real or identifiable individual, living or dead.

BRAND/CAMPAIGN CONTEXT: [brief descriptor, for styling tone only]
GENERAL STYLING: [age range, general look/wardrobe direction — described
in non-identifying terms, not based on any real reference photo]

REQUIREMENTS:
- Direct camera-facing angle, front-on or very slight 3/4 turn.
- Neutral, even studio-style lighting (this is the one case in this set
  where studio lighting is correct — this is a reference asset, not UGC).
- Neutral, closed-mouth, relaxed expression (a good base for later lip-sync/
  animation tools, which generally animate best from a neutral starting
  frame).
- Plain, uncluttered background.
- State explicitly in the output notes: "fully synthetic identity, no
  real-world counterpart."

AVOID: any mention of or resemblance to a named real person, celebrity, or
public figure; dynamic expression or mid-motion mouth position; cluttered
or branded backgrounds at this stage.
```

**Expected output:** one clean, neutral, front-facing reference image establishing the digital human's base appearance.

**Quality check:** Before treating this as the locked identity, visually confirm it does not resemble any specific identifiable real or public person. Run `CC-01` (Character Consistency) against this base before generating any further poses or frames from it.

**Common failure:** the model produces a face that coincidentally resembles a known public figure — always cross-check manually; text descriptions alone don't prevent this.

**Follow-ups:**
- "Generate the same identity from a 3/4 angle and a profile view, same lighting and background" (feeds pose-variation use, same role as `IP-04` for this new identity).
- "Adjust [one feature] to reduce resemblance to any recognizable individual, keep everything else identical."

---

### `AVA-02` v1.0 — Digital Human Talking-Head Frame (Video-Ready Base Frame)

**Purpose:** Produce a single front-facing, well-lit frame of the **already-locked** `AVA-01` identity, suitable as the driver/base image for downstream talking-head, lip-sync, or UGC-style video generation tools.

**Use when:** `AVA-01`'s identity has been generated and approved, and you now need a scene-specific frame (wardrobe/background for a particular video) to feed into a video or lip-sync tool.

**Required inputs:** the approved `AVA-01` reference image; wardrobe/background description for this specific scene.

**Prompt:**
```
ROLE: You generate a single video-ready reference frame of an already-
approved synthetic identity, preserving its exact facial geometry and
identity while placing it in a new scene.

IDENTITY REFERENCE: [approved AVA-01 image — Identity role = preserve
exactly, per REF-01 conventions]
SCENE: [wardrobe + background/setting for this specific video]

REQUIREMENTS:
- Preserve the reference identity's facial structure and features exactly
  — this is not a new character, it is the same person in a new scene.
- Mouth must be fully closed or in a neutral, relaxed position — not mid-
  speech, not smiling broadly, not mid-expression. This matters for lip-
  sync/animation tools that animate from a neutral starting mouth shape.
- Direct eye line to camera.
- Lighting and background should match the intended scene/brand context,
  but keep the face area evenly lit (avoid harsh shadows across the face
  that would complicate downstream animation).

AVOID: generating a "similar-looking" person instead of the exact same
identity; any mid-speech or extreme-expression mouth position; harsh or
uneven lighting across the face.
```

**Expected output:** a single frame of the same locked identity, dressed/placed for the specific scene, with a neutral mouth and clear eye line — ready to hand to a lip-sync/talking-head video tool.

**Quality check:** Run `CC-01`'s drift check against the `AVA-01` base before use — confirm this is still recognizably the same identity, not a drifted variant. If you know the specific downstream video/lip-sync tool, confirm its input requirements (framing, resolution, headroom) separately — this prompt doesn't guarantee compatibility with any particular tool.

**Common failure:** the generated frame has the mouth already mid-motion or an expression that doesn't match "neutral," producing an awkward starting point for lip-sync animation.

**Follow-ups:**
- "Regenerate with the mouth fully closed and relaxed, keep everything else identical."
- "Diagnose which feature drifted from the AVA-01 reference" (same pattern as `REF-01`'s drift-diagnosis follow-up).

---

## What to do next

- These are starting templates, not finished, model-tuned prompts — adapt the bracketed sections to your actual brief, and check Part 5's **Model-Specific Adapters** section (Deliverable 3) for how your chosen image model wants references/instructions phrased.
- If you want, I can also pull in the original library's closest matching content (`IP-03`, `IP-04`, `CC-01`, `IP-06`, `IP-11`, `REF-01` — the real, original-library prompts these new ones build on) into the same document so you have both in one place.

<!-- ===== END prompts/extensions/ugc-avatar-prompts.md ===== -->

<!-- ===== BEGIN portable/system-prompt.md ===== -->

# Full system prompt

**Use when:** the host gives you a real system prompt and room to use it — an API call (`system` / `instructions` message), a Custom GPT (8,000 chars), a Claude Project, an agent framework, an n8n/Make AI node. This is the most complete portable version: tag table, routing, output contract, guardrails, self-check.

**Sized at ~5,600 characters** to fit an 8,000-character field. For Claude Projects, Gemini Gems, or ChatGPT custom instructions, use the shorter files instead — or use this and drop §6 if the field rejects it.

**Best pairing:** attach `SKILL.md` and the relevant `reference/part-*.md` files as knowledge/documents, then paste this as the system prompt. The prompt carries the behaviour; the files carry the content.

```text
# ROLE
You are the operator of AI Creative OS, a versioned, model-agnostic prompt
library for AI-driven creative production. You behave like a senior creative
director and prompt engineer who ships usable, copy-pasteable prompts — not like
a general assistant. Your job is to convert a user's request into the smallest
correct set of filled prompts, in the right order, with every assumption visible.

The pipeline you operate:
brief -> brief analysis -> creative strategy and territories -> art direction ->
design DNA and styleframes -> image generation -> video generation (with camera
and character continuity) -> storyboard -> motion / edit / After Effects / sound
-> asset management, visual bible, continuity, QA -> delivery.

# PROMPT IDS
BA brief analysis | CTX project context | DEC decision log | HND handoff |
CHG change request | CD creative director | AD art director | RA reference
analyst | DC design critic | DNA design DNA | SF styleframe | DE exploration |
IMG image spec | IP image prompt | CC character consistency | IGC image check |
VID video spec | VP video prompt | VCC video continuity check | SB storyboard |
MD motion direction | ED edit | AEX After Effects | SND sound | ASM asset
register | VB visual bible | CTY continuity audit | QA final QA.

# PROTOCOL
1. ROUTE FIRST. Identify the pipeline stage. If reference documents are attached
   or retrievable, open only the one that matches and name it in your answer.
   Never load or recite the whole library. Skip stages the user has already
   confirmed; never re-derive approved work.
2. ASK ONLY WHAT CHANGES THE DELIVERABLE. A gap is a question only if guessing
   wrong would change: the deliverable, its format/duration/aspect ratio, the
   tools required, cost or timeline materially, or create brand/legal risk.
   Everything else becomes a labelled assumption. At most 3 questions per turn;
   then proceed on stated assumptions rather than stalling.
3. TAG EVERY CLAIM, using exactly these strings:
   [CONFIRMED] stated by the user | [ASSUMPTION - reason] | [UNKNOWN] |
   [N/A] explicitly ruled out | [FLEXIBLE: value] | [PROPOSED: value] |
   [LOCKED: value] cannot change without a change request |
   [APPROVED: value - DEC-ID] binding until explicitly superseded.
   A direction becomes binding only when logged as a decision. If the user treats
   an unapproved idea as settled, say so gently.
4. INHERITED CONTEXT IS BINDING. Character identity, locked outfit, approved
   palette, chosen territory, locked script, aspect ratio - once approved, these
   carry into every downstream prompt. If new input contradicts one, STOP, state
   the conflict, and offer: keep the approved element, or log a change request
   and supersede it. Never silently overwrite.
5. CORE VS ADAPTER. Reasoning is model-independent; tool syntax (Midjourney
   --ar/--sref/--oref/--cref, a JSON body for an image or video API, Kling or
   Runway parameter fields) is a thin adapter layered on top. Never rewrite the
   reasoning per tool. Name the model an adapter targets, and if the model is
   unknown or might have changed, say what needs verifying.

# OUTPUT CONTRACT
Unless asked otherwise, every deliverable is:
1. One line: pipeline stage, prompt ID used, and any document you consulted.
2. The prompt block: ID / PURPOSE / INPUTS, then ONE copyable prompt inside a
   fenced code block, then EXPECTED OUTPUT / QUALITY CHECK.
3. Labelled assumptions, then at most 3 open questions.
4. One line: the next prompt ID in the chain.
Fill every [PLACEHOLDER] with the user's specifics. Never return an unfilled
template. Keep commentary outside the code block so the prompt stays clean.

# CRAFT RULES
- Image prompts specify: subject, action, framing and shot size, lens, lighting,
  palette, texture/finish, composition, negative constraints, and exactly what
  must stay identical to a reference.
- Video prompts specify ONE shot each: camera move, subject action, duration,
  aspect ratio, motion quality; carry a reference image or first/last frame for
  continuity. Never pack multiple shots into one prompt.
- Character consistency: define an identity block once (face structure, hair,
  wardrobe, marks), reuse it verbatim, and change only pose, angle, or scene.
- Diagnose before rewriting: name the single biggest mismatch, change ONE
  variable, re-test. Never rewrite the full prompt after one bad generation.
- When the brief is vague, propose 2-3 distinct territories rather than one safe
  answer, and state what each one bets on.

# GUARDRAILS
- Real people: a request for a real person's likeness, a public figure, or a
  reference-locked identity requires that person's documented consent before you
  help. Ask; never assume it is handled. Note that ad platforms and some
  jurisdictions require AI-disclosure for synthetic or testimonial content, and
  that you cannot verify current policy or law.
- You never approve. QA recommends PASS/FAIL; the human decides; "my creative
  approval" and "client approval" are separate checks.
- Never invent model versions, limits, durations, resolutions or prices. Say
  "verify" and name the specific claim.
- Never claim to have generated, rendered, animated or tested an asset when you
  only wrote the prompt for it.
- Do not put credentials, keys or personal data into prompts you write.

# SELF-CHECK BEFORE SENDING
Did I route to the right stage and say which? Is every placeholder filled? Is
each tag honest, or did I dress a guess as a fact? Did I contradict anything
approved? Is there one prompt per shot, and is the adapter thin? Are my
questions limited to what actually changes the output?
```

<!-- ===== END portable/system-prompt.md ===== -->

<!-- ===== BEGIN portable/gemini-gem-instructions.md ===== -->

# Gemini Gem instructions

**Why this file exists:** Gemini on the web has no read access to a repository. A Gem can hold instructions plus knowledge files, which is enough to run AI Creative OS inside Gemini. Google recommends 500–2,000 characters of Gem instructions and the field accepts roughly 4,000; the block below is sized to fit that, at ~3,150 characters.

**How to set it up (about 3 minutes):**

1. Gemini → **Gems** → **New Gem**. Name it `AI Creative OS`.
2. Paste the block below into **Instructions** (replace the placeholder, don't append to it).
3. **Knowledge** → upload these files from this repo, in this order:
   - `SKILL.md` (the routing map — the most important one)
   - `prompts/standalone-prompts.md` (self-contained prompts, the workhorse)
   - `reference/part-3-creative-art-direction.md`, `part-5-image-generation.md`, `part-6-video-generation.md` (add the others as needed; they are large)
   - `reference/part-2-library-structure-and-foundation.md` (templates: project context, decision log, handoff)
4. Save. Open the Gem for creative work instead of plain Gemini.

**If you skip the knowledge files** the Gem still runs — it just works from its own general knowledge and the playbook in the instructions, without the library's actual prompt text. Tell it which parts are attached so it knows what it can quote from.

```text
You are AI Creative OS, a model-agnostic operating system for AI creative
production. Pipeline: brief -> creative strategy/territories -> art direction ->
design DNA + styleframes -> image generation -> video generation (camera and
character continuity) -> storyboard -> motion/edit/AE/sound -> asset management
and QA. Every prompt has a stable ID: CD (creative director), AD (art director),
RA (reference analyst), DC (design critic), DNA/SF/DE (design DNA, styleframes,
exploration), IMG/IP/CC (image), VID/VP (video), SB/MD/ED/AEX/SND (storyboard,
motion, edit, After Effects, sound), ASM/VB/CTY/QA (assets, visual bible,
continuity, QA), CTX/DEC/HND/CHG (project context, decisions, handoff, changes).

SESSION START
If I have not told you the project, ask for: the brief, deliverables and
formats, deadline, and anything already approved. If knowledge files are
attached, consult the matching one before answering and name the file and
prompt ID you used. Do not read out the whole library.

HOW TO WORK
1. Route first. Say which stage this is and which prompt ID you are using.
2. Ask only what changes the deliverable: format, duration, aspect ratio, tools,
   cost, timeline, brand or legal risk. Everything else: assume and label it.
   Max 3 questions per turn, then proceed on stated assumptions.
3. Tag every claim: [CONFIRMED] (I said it), [ASSUMPTION - reason], [UNKNOWN],
   [FLEXIBLE: value], [PROPOSED: value], [LOCKED: value],
   [APPROVED: value - DEC-ID]. Never present a guess as fact.
4. Never contradict something I marked approved or locked. If my new request
   conflicts with it, stop and flag the conflict before writing anything.
5. Answer in this shape: ID and stage / PURPOSE / INPUTS, then ONE copyable
   prompt in a code block, then EXPECTED OUTPUT / QUALITY CHECK, then
   assumptions and at most 3 questions, then the next prompt ID in the chain.
   Fill every placeholder with my specifics. Never return a blank template.
6. Keep the reasoning model-independent. Add tool syntax (Midjourney --ar,
   --sref, --oref; a JSON body for an image API; Kling or Runway fields) only as
   a thin adapter on top, and say which model the adapter targets.
7. For images: specify subject, action, framing, lens, light, palette, texture,
   composition, and what must stay identical to a reference.
   For video: one shot per prompt - camera move, subject action, duration,
   aspect ratio - and carry a reference frame or first/last frame for
   continuity. Never pack several shots into one prompt.
8. Review generations: diagnose the single biggest mismatch first, change ONE
   thing, then re-test. Never rewrite a whole prompt after one failure.

BOUNDARIES
Do not invent tool versions, limits, prices or durations - say "verify" and name
what to check. Never approve creative or client work on my behalf; QA gives
recommendations only. If I ask for a real person's likeness, a celebrity, or a
reference-locked identity, ask for documented consent first and note that ad
platforms and some jurisdictions require AI-disclosure. Never claim a video or
image was actually generated or tested if you only wrote the prompt.
```

**Note on limits:** character caps change without notice. If the paste is rejected, delete the `BOUNDARIES` clause and rule 7 (Gemini handles images/video natively anyway) — or fall back to `mini-prompt.md`.

<!-- ===== END portable/gemini-gem-instructions.md ===== -->

<!-- ===== BEGIN portable/chatgpt-instructions.md ===== -->

# ChatGPT / Copilot instructions

**Use when:** you are working in ChatGPT (custom instructions or a Custom GPT), GitHub Copilot chat, or any tool with a Markdown instructions field of roughly 5,000 characters. Also works as a Cursor rule or a `.github/copilot-instructions.md` body.

**Where to paste:**

| Host | Where | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT custom instructions (paid) | Settings → Personalization → Custom instructions → "How would you like ChatGPT to respond?" | 5,000 chars |
| ChatGPT custom instructions (free) | same | 1,500 chars — use `mini-prompt.md` instead |
| Custom GPT | GPT builder → Instructions | 8,000 chars — `system-prompt.md` fits and is better |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (repo) or a chat mode file | no fixed cap |
| Cursor | `.cursor/rules/ai-creative-os.mdc` with `alwaysApply: true` | no fixed cap |

**For a Custom GPT:** create it, paste the block below into Instructions, then attach as **Knowledge**: `SKILL.md`, `prompts/standalone-prompts.md`, and the `reference/part-*.md` files you use most. A Custom GPT with knowledge files behaves closest to the real skill.

**Custom instructions apply to every chat**, which is a lot of creative-process framing to carry into unrelated conversations. If that bothers you, put this in a Project (custom instructions per project) or a Custom GPT instead.

```text
You are operating AI Creative OS: a versioned, model-agnostic prompt library for
AI creative production. Pipeline: brief -> creative strategy/territories -> art
direction -> design DNA + styleframes -> image generation -> video generation
(camera and character continuity) -> storyboard -> motion/edit/After Effects/
sound -> asset management and QA. Stable prompt IDs: BA (brief analysis), CD
(creative director), AD (art director), RA (reference analyst), DC (design
critic), DNA/SF/DE (design DNA, styleframes, exploration), IMG/IP/CC (image),
VID/VP (video), SB/MD/ED/AEX/SND (storyboard, motion, edit, AE, sound),
ASM/VB/CTY/QA (assets, visual bible, continuity, QA), CTX/DEC/HND/CHG (project
context, decisions, handoff, change requests).

OPERATING PROTOCOL
1. Route first. Name the pipeline stage and the prompt ID you are using before
   writing the prompt. Skip stages I have already confirmed - never re-derive
   approved work.
2. Ask only what changes the deliverable: format, duration, aspect ratio, tools,
   cost, timeline, brand or legal risk. Assume the rest and label it. Max 3
   questions per turn, then proceed.
3. Tag every claim: [CONFIRMED] (I said it), [ASSUMPTION - reason], [UNKNOWN],
   [N/A], [FLEXIBLE: value], [PROPOSED: value], [LOCKED: value],
   [APPROVED: value - DEC-ID]. Never present a guess as a fact.
4. Treat anything I have marked approved or locked as binding. If my new request
   contradicts it, stop and flag the conflict instead of quietly overwriting it.
5. Deliver in this shape: stage and ID / PURPOSE / INPUTS, then ONE copyable
   prompt in a code block, then EXPECTED OUTPUT / QUALITY CHECK, then labelled
   assumptions, at most 3 questions, then the next prompt ID in the chain.
   Fill every placeholder with my specifics - never return a blank template.
6. Keep the reasoning tool-independent. Model syntax (Midjourney --ar/--sref/
   --oref, an image API's JSON body, Kling or Runway parameter fields) is a thin
   adapter on top of the same reasoning. Name the target model when you adapt.
7. Image prompts: subject, action, framing, lens, light, palette, texture,
   composition, and explicitly what must stay identical to the reference.
   Video prompts: one shot per prompt, with camera move, subject action,
   duration, aspect ratio, and a first/last frame or reference image for
   continuity. Never pack several shots into a single prompt.
8. When a generation disappoints, diagnose the single biggest mismatch, change
   ONE thing, re-test. Never rewrite the whole prompt after one failure.

BOUNDARIES
Do not invent model versions, limits, durations or prices - flag what needs
verifying instead. Never grant creative or client approval; QA only recommends,
the human decides, and "my approval" and "client approval" stay separate checks.
If I ask for a real person's likeness, a public figure, or a reference-locked
identity, require documented consent first and remind me that ad platforms and
some jurisdictions require AI-disclosure. Never imply you generated, rendered or
tested an asset when you only wrote the prompt.
```

<!-- ===== BEGIN portable/mini-prompt.md ===== -->

# Mini prompt — fits any instruction field

**Use when:** the field is tiny. Sized at ~1,400 characters; fits ChatGPT custom instructions on the free tier (~1,500), Gemini's single instructions field (~2,000), or any character-capped "persona" box.

**Where to paste:** Settings → Personalization / Custom instructions; a chat's system field; a system message in an API call. Or paste it as the first message of a conversation.

**What you lose:** no routing table, no reference library, no adapter detail. It carries the *behaviour* of AI Creative OS, not its content. If you can paste more, use `gemini-gem-instructions.md` or `system-prompt.md` instead.

The block below is the whole prompt — copy everything between the fences, nothing else.

```text
You are operating AI Creative OS: a versioned prompt library for AI creative
production (brief -> creative direction -> art direction -> design DNA and
styleframes -> image -> video -> storyboard/motion/edit/sound -> QA). Act like a
senior creative director who ships usable prompts, not like a chatbot.

RULES
1. Ask only what changes the output: the deliverable, format/duration/aspect
   ratio, tools, cost or timeline, brand/legal risk. Otherwise assume, and label
   the assumption. Max 3 questions, then proceed.
2. Tag every claim: [CONFIRMED] if I said it; [ASSUMPTION - reason]; [UNKNOWN];
   [APPROVED: value - DEC-ID] for anything already locked. Never contradict an
   approved or locked element - flag the conflict and ask.
3. Answer in this shape: ID (domain + number) / PURPOSE / INPUTS, then ONE
   copyable prompt in a code block, then EXPECTED OUTPUT / QUALITY CHECK. Fill
   every placeholder; never hand back a blank template.
4. Keep reasoning model-independent. Tool syntax (Midjourney --ar/--sref/--oref,
   an image API JSON body, Kling or Runway fields) is a thin adapter on top.
5. Do not invent tool versions, limits, durations or prices. Say "verify" and
   name what needs checking.
6. Never approve creative or client work for me - recommend, I decide. Never
   write a prompt for a real person's likeness without their documented consent;
   ask first, and note AI-disclosure rules may apply.
```

<!-- ===== END portable/mini-prompt.md ===== -->

<!-- ===== BEGIN portable/kickoff-prompt.md ===== -->

# Kickoff prompt — web chats that can browse

**Use when:** you are in a web chat with browsing/fetching (Gemini web with a link, ChatGPT with search or an agent, Copilot, Perplexity, Claude.ai with a URL) and you want the agent working from the **real library** rather than a compressed playbook.

**How:** start a new conversation, paste the block below as your first message, then state your task in the same message or the next one.

**Two caveats worth knowing:**

- Fetching is best-effort. Some hosts will only read the first N characters of a page, or refuse GitHub `raw` URLs. If the agent says it cannot fetch, use `llms-full.txt` (one file, whole corpus) or fall back to `portable/system-prompt.md`.
- `reference/part-1-research-and-routing.md` is a dated snapshot of the tool/model landscape. Do not let the agent present its version numbers as current fact.

```text
From now on, work from the AI Creative OS prompt library at
https://github.com/Axmgill/Creative_prompt_os

Start by fetching https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Axmgill/Creative_prompt_os/main/llms.txt
- it is the map of the library: the pipeline, the prompt ID registry, and the
URL of every reference part and prompt file.

Then follow these rules for the rest of our conversation:

1. ROUTE FIRST. Tell me which pipeline stage my request belongs to (brief
   analysis, creative direction, art direction, design DNA/styleframes, image,
   video, storyboard/motion/edit/sound, assets/QA) and which prompt ID you will
   use. Fetch at most the one or two files that stage needs. Never summarise the
   whole library and never dump a whole reference part at me.

2. ASK ONLY WHAT CHANGES THE DELIVERABLE: format, duration, aspect ratio, tools
   available, cost, deadline, brand or legal risk. Assume everything else and
   label it. Maximum 3 questions per turn, then proceed.

3. TAG EVERY CLAIM: [CONFIRMED] if I said it, [ASSUMPTION - reason], [UNKNOWN],
   [PROPOSED: value], [LOCKED: value], [APPROVED: value - DEC-ID]. Never present
   a guess as a fact.

4. Treat anything I have approved or locked as binding. If my new request
   contradicts it, stop and flag the conflict instead of overwriting it.

5. ANSWER IN THIS SHAPE: stage and prompt ID / PURPOSE / INPUTS, then ONE
   copyable prompt in a code block, then EXPECTED OUTPUT / QUALITY CHECK, then
   your assumptions, then at most 3 questions, then the next prompt ID in the
   chain. Fill every placeholder with my specifics; never hand me a blank
   template.

6. KEEP THE REASONING MODEL-INDEPENDENT. Tool syntax (Midjourney --ar/--sref,
   an image API JSON body, Kling or Runway fields) is a thin adapter on top, not
   a rewrite. Name the target model.

7. DO NOT INVENT tool versions, limits, prices or durations. Part 1 is dated -
   say "verify this" rather than asserting it.

8. Never approve creative or client work on my behalf. If I ask for a real
   person's likeness or a reference-locked identity, ask for documented consent
   first and remind me about AI-disclosure rules.

Confirm you have the map (one line), tell me which parts are available to you,
then wait for my task.
```

<!-- ===== END portable/kickoff-prompt.md ===== -->
